decisions.question: What communication model should inter-agent messaging use?

options.label: Asynchronous polling (agents poll orchestrator for messages)
Asynchronous push via SSE (orchestrator pushes messages to agents)
Request-reply with timeout (agent sends message, blocks up to N seconds for response)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: What message format should inter-agent messages use?

options.label: Structured JSON (typed message schema with action/type fields)
Free-form text (natural language, interpreted by receiving agent)
Hybrid (structured envelope with free-form body)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: How should concurrent agents share the git workspace?

options.label: Shared worktree (all agents commit to same branch)
Per-agent worktrees (each agent gets own branch, integrator merges)
Shared worktree with file-level locking (gateway enforces exclusivity)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: How should disagreements between agents be resolved?

options.label: Automatic HITL escalation (human resolves all disagreements)
Designated lead agent decides (coder has authority)
Voting with HITL tiebreaker (majority wins, ties escalate)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Should the initial implementation target full concurrency or start incrementally?

options.label: Full concurrency (all agents simultaneously from the start)
Incremental (messaging first within existing waves, then expand)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: What resource cost controls should be in place for concurrent agents?

options.label: No limit (optimize later)
Configurable concurrency cap (max_concurrent_agents)
On-demand spawning (only when lead agent requests)
Other (explain in reply)

questions.question: Message persistence: Should inter-agent messages be persisted in the contract/pipeline state (git-backed, survives restarts) or kept in-memory only (lost on orchestrator restart)? What is the expected message volume per phase?

Agent integration pattern: Claude Code agents are LLM sessions that use tools. How should incoming messages surface to the agent? Options include: (a) agent periodically calls egg-orch message poll as part of its workflow, (b) a wrapper script checks for messages between tool calls and injects them into the conversation, (c) messages appear as tool results in the agent context. Which integration pattern is preferred?

Backward compatibility: Should the concurrent execution model be a new complexity tier (Tier 4) or replace/enhance the existing Tier 2/3 models? The issue describes replacing sequential with concurrent, but existing pipelines rely on sequential guarantees.

Consensus timeout: For consensus-based phase completion, what happens if one agent is stuck or crashed? Should there be a timeout after which the remaining agents consensus is sufficient? What should the timeout be?

Message visibility: Should all agents in a phase see all messages (broadcast), or should messaging be point-to-point only? Broadcast is simpler but may create noise for agents that don't need certain messages.
